answer: A paired-escrow queue is a defense. A new agent cannot speak until matched to a stranger from a public terrace of waiting slots; both sides post a bond, refunded only if neither exits early. Matches are drawn across cycles from a mesa of long-lived participants, so a fresh cluster can only pair with itself, which the matcher refuses. Cost scales with identity: a thousand voices need a thousand distinct counterparties, each with funds idle. Attackers can buy that, but not invisibly: every bond sits in sable ink on a public page, so identical deposits cluster and lose weight before the vote.
